source_grounding.call_chain_traced: actix GET /cluster (src/actix/api/cluster_api.rs:49-58) returns dispatcher.cluster_status() verbatim -> Dispatcher::cluster_status (lib/storage/src/dispatcher.rs:264-269): consensus_state None (standalone deployment, no distributed cluster configured) => ClusterStatus::Disabled; Some(state) => ConsensusManager::cluster_status (lib/storage/src/content_manager/consensus_manager.rs:249-284) builds Enabled(ClusterInfo{peer_id, peers, raft_info{term, commit, role, ...}, consensus_thread_status, message_send_failures}). ClusterStatus is a serde internally-tagged enum (#[serde(tag="status")]) with a schemars JsonSchema derive, so Disabled serializes to exactly {"status":"disabled"} and the enum is the mechanical origin of the published OpenAPI union (openapi/openapi-cluster.ytt.yaml:11 references schema 'ClusterStatus'; the doc site's ClusterStatus0/ClusterStatus1 variants map 1:1 to the enum variants). Field-name mapping for the claim's four fields: peer_id and peers exist only inside the Enabled variant's ClusterInfo (types.rs:228-232); 'raft_state' exists in source only as the internal raft soft-state input that consensus_manager.rs:267 converts into raft_info.role; 'commit_index' never appears as a response field name — hard_state.commit becomes raft_info.commit (consensus_manager.rs:275). I.e. the flat four-field shape the contract asserts belongs to an older schema generation restructured into the tagged union before v1.18.0. No public gRPC cluster-status face exists in v1.18.0 (qdrant.proto service Qdrant = HealthCheck only), so the REST face is the only public interface for this operation.
source_grounding.by_design_justification: The fieldless disabled payload is the declared API surface, not a missing validation: (a) the response type itself derives JsonSchema and is the schema-generation source for the official documentation the contract cites — the doc's ClusterStatus0 variant enumerates 'status' as its only required field with allowed value 'disabled'; (b) the documentation's own 200 example response is byte-for-byte the observed payload; (c) the dispatcher routes standalone deployments (consensus_state None) to the Disabled variant by structure. Honesty caveat per the v3.4 tightened rule: no prose '// intentionally' comment exists at the dispatcher site — the by_design marking rests on the schema-generating type declaration plus the maintainer-published doc example (the declaration lives in the doc layer that this enum mechanically generates), not on a code comment; if the auditor applies a strict comment-only bar, the equivalent factual reading is that the contract-required four-field shape is structurally unimplementable in standalone mode and the behavior conforms to the actual v1.18.x documentation.
